questions.q: What is the maximum power allowed for a motorcycle on an A2-grade licence?
options: {{fact:licence.a2.max_kw}}
No power limit
{{fact:licence.a1.max_kw}}
22 kilowatts
questions.explain: On an A2 licence, power is limited to {{fact:licence.a2.max_kw}} (and also to a power-to-weight ratio of up to 0.1 kilowatts per kg), under regulation 176.

questions.q: What is the maximum engine capacity allowed for a motorcycle on an A2 licence?
options: 50 cc
250 cc
{{fact:licence.a2.max_cc}}
There's no capacity limit on A2
questions.explain: An A2 licence is limited to a motorcycle with an engine capacity of up to {{fact:licence.a2.max_cc}} (regulation 176), in addition to the power limit.

questions.q: What is the minimum age for obtaining an A licence (a motorcycle with no power limit)?
options: {{fact:licence.a.min_age}}
questions.explain: An A licence, which doesn't limit the motorcycle's power, is granted from at least age {{fact:licence.a.min_age}} (regulation 189(g)).

questions.q: What does a holder of an A1 licence need in order to get an A licence?
options: No requirement — you can apply immediately
At least {{fact:licence.a.seniority_a1}} of seniority on the A1 licence
Five years of seniority on the A1 licence
Just another theory test, with no seniority requirement
questions.explain: To move from A1 to A, you need at least {{fact:licence.a.seniority_a1}} of seniority on the A1 licence (regulation 189(g)).

questions.q: Who must wear a fastened protective helmet on a motorcycle, and when?
options: Only when it's raining
Only the rider, and only on a non-urban road
Only the passenger
Both the rider and the passenger, at all times
questions.explain: A fastened protective helmet covering the ear is compulsory for both the rider and the passenger on a motorcycle, at all times and on every road (regulation 119(c)).

questions.q: What is the main difference between a full-face helmet and an open-face helmet?
options: An open-face helmet is legal only for the passenger
A full-face helmet is lighter in weight
There's no difference in protection, only in appearance
A full-face helmet also covers the chin and gives more protection in a crash
questions.explain: A full-face helmet covers the whole head including the chin, which is hit frequently in motorcycle falls, and gives the greatest protection.

questions.q: What is the fine and points for driving or riding a motorcycle without a helmet?
options: {{fine:motorcycle-no-helmet}} and {{points:motorcycle-no-helmet}} points
{{fine:phone-handheld}} and {{points:phone-handheld}} points
No fine, just a warning
{{fine:bicycle-helmet-cyclist}} and no points
questions.explain: Driving or riding a motorcycle without a helmet incurs {{fine:motorcycle-no-helmet}} and {{points:motorcycle-no-helmet}} points.

questions.q: Beyond the helmet, which protective gear helps most in a slide on the road?
options: A dark-coloured shirt
A wool cap under the helmet
Dark sunglasses
A jacket and gloves padded at the shoulders, elbows and knuckles
questions.explain: A slide is far more common than a head-on impact on a motorcycle; a padded jacket and gloves protect the areas hit first in a slide on asphalt.

questions.q: On the rider's right hand you'll find —
options: The clutch lever and the front brake lever
The throttle grip and the front brake lever
The throttle grip and the gear pedal
Only the throttle grip, with no brake
questions.explain: The right hand has the throttle grip and the front brake lever; the clutch lever is on the left hand, and the gear pedal is under the left foot.

questions.q: How do you operate the throttle grip to accelerate?
options: Pull it backward
Push it forward
Twist it toward the rider
Press it downward
questions.explain: Twisting the throttle grip toward the rider accelerates; releasing the twist slows down.

questions.q: What must you make sure of before setting off on a motorcycle that was standing on a stand?
options: That the gear pedal is locked in a high gear
That the stand (side or centre) is fully raised
That the mirrors are aimed only backward
That the helmet is worn, without fastening it
questions.explain: A side or centre stand that isn't fully raised can strike the road in a turn and tip the motorcycle over.

questions.q: How many mutually independent brake systems must a motorcycle have?
options: Only one, on the rear wheel
Two: one on the front wheel and one on the rear
Three, including a separate hand brake
There's no minimum requirement in law
questions.explain: Regulation 328 requires two independent brake systems — one on the front wheel and one on the rear (or the two rear wheels on a tricycle), each able to decelerate the motorcycle by at least 1.5 metres per second squared.

questions.q: Which brake accounts for most of the braking power on a motorcycle?
options: The front brake
Both brakes always contribute exactly equally
The rear brake
It depends only on the rider's weight
questions.explain: Under braking, the weight of the motorcycle and rider shifts forward and increases the front wheel's grip, which is why it accounts for most of the braking power.

questions.q: What is the risk of squeezing the front brake hard while the motorcycle is leaned over in a turn?
options: It activates ABS even on a motorcycle without the system
It improves grip in the turn
The front wheel can slide out and the motorcycle can fall
The motorcycle will slow down too fast, with no extra risk
questions.explain: Hard front braking while leaned over increases the chance of the front wheel sliding out — first straighten up as much as possible, and only then brake hard.

questions.q: What does ABS do on a motorcycle during emergency braking?
options: Brakes the motorcycle by itself without the rider's involvement
Prevents the wheels from locking, and reduces the risk of a fall under hard braking
Operates only the rear brake
Always halves the stopping distance
questions.explain: ABS prevents wheel lock under hard braking; on a motorcycle this is critical, because a locked wheel can bring the motorcycle down, not just extend the stopping distance.

questions.q: How do you turn right on a motorcycle at normal road speed?
options: Forcefully turn the handlebar left
Brake gently during the turn
Push the right handlebar grip lightly forward — counter-steering
Lean the body left without touching the handlebars
questions.explain: Above walking pace, a turn begins with counter-steering: a light push on the handlebar grip in the direction of the turn makes the motorcycle lean the same way.

questions.q: What happens to the lean angle as a turn gets sharper or the speed gets higher?
options: It decreases
It always stays constant
It becomes negative
It increases
questions.explain: The sharper the turn or the higher the speed, the greater the motorcycle's lean angle.

questions.q: Where should you look inside a turn on a motorcycle?
options: Far ahead, toward where you want to end up
Straight at the ground right in front of the front wheel
Only at the rear mirror
It doesn't matter — your eyes don't affect the riding line
questions.explain: A motorcycle tends to go where the rider is looking; looking far ahead toward where you want to end up improves the line through the turn.

questions.q: When should you slow down before a sharp turn?
options: Only if you see a vehicle ahead of you
Before the turn, before the motorcycle leans over
There's no need to slow down before a familiar turn
Within the turn itself, gradually
questions.explain: Braking within a turn, when the motorcycle is already leaned over, increases the risk of sliding — slow down before the turn, not inside it.

questions.q: What does regulation 122 establish about riding alongside another vehicle on a motorcycle?
options: It's forbidden, except to overtake the other vehicle or lawfully pass it
Allowed only alongside a bicycle, forbidden alongside a motor vehicle
Always allowed, even as a regular way to move through a jam
Completely forbidden in every situation, even while overtaking
questions.explain: Regulation 122 bans a motorcyclist from riding alongside another vehicle, including a bicycle or another motorcycle, except to overtake it or lawfully pass it — there's no permission for regular lane filtering.

questions.q: When is a holder of an A2 licence allowed to carry a passenger on the motorcycle?
options: Only after a full year with the licence, with no age condition
Carrying a passenger is absolutely forbidden on an A2 licence
Only from age 18, and after holding the licence for at least two months — whichever is later
From the very first day with the licence, at any age
questions.explain: A holder of an A2 or A1 licence may not carry a passenger unless they have turned 18 or have held the licence for at least two months — whichever is later (regulation 120(c)).

questions.q: When must a motorcycle ride with its headlight on?
options: Always — by day and by night alike
Only on a non-urban road
Only at night
Only during “lighting hours”, like other vehicles
questions.explain: Unlike other motor vehicles, a motorcycle must ride with its headlight lit at all times — by day and by night alike (regulation 97(b)).

questions.q: Where should a motorcyclist position themselves within the lane?
options: Right up against the right dividing line, always
Right up close to the vehicle ahead, to be seen better
Always exactly in the centre of the lane, without moving
Wherever gives the best forward visibility and visibility to other drivers, changing position as needed
questions.explain: Oil and grime build up in the centre of the lane; the right position is whichever gives the best visibility and gives the best chance of being seen, and it changes with the situation.

questions.q: What is the risk of a drive chain that's too loose or worn?
options: It has no effect at all on braking or the drivetrain
It only causes higher fuel consumption
It can catch in the rear wheel and lock it
It's only noisy, with no safety risk
questions.explain: A chain that's too loose or damaged can catch in the rear sprocket and lock it while riding — an immediate risk, not just a fault to fix later.

questions.q: Why is it especially important to keep the correct tyre pressure on a motorcycle?
options: Because the law bans riding with a varying tyre pressure
It only affects the speedometer
Because motorcycle tyres can't be replaced
Because a motorcycle has only two contact points with the road, much smaller than a car's
questions.explain: A motorcycle has only two small contact points with the road, so tyre condition and pressure affect stability and braking far more than in a car.
